status: native ARM64 bridge foundation rebuilt and mock protocol tests passed; real BE19000AI ASUS startup is not yet ported or accepted
scope: Local source and evidence review; new reusable bridge source/test files and build artifacts only. No existing source checkout, rootfs, configuration, device, active unit, router, firmware slot or Git commit changed. No actual ASUS daemon was executed.
board_scope: GT-BE19000AI BCM/B53 runs Ubuntu/systemd; its SL1680 AI board remains a separate OS. BCM AI-control functions must continue working without coupling ordinary radio/web actions to AI reboot/upgrade.

startup_blockers.evidence: The init/preinit applets dispatch init_main; rc start/stop/restart signal PID1; service functions use getpid()!=1 to forward work instead of doing it. AI tftpd has its own PID1 test beyond the old BE98 port.
startup_blockers.required_change: Call leon_rc_manager_enter before any board effects; replace only explicit manager-role predicates with leon_rc_is_manager in the actually selected BE19000AI source/object set. Keep real getpid semantics and ensure fork children do not inherit manager authority. Rebuild rc and statically retained call sites with precise linker wrappers; do not merely change the unit Type or daemonize stock rc.

startup_blockers.evidence: sysinit creates the old tmp/etc and var tree, changes umask and /tmp mode, truncates hosts/fstab, symlinks rom/etc entries, replaces resolv.conf and invokes ldconfig. setup_passwd follows later. The BE98 patch only guards fstab in the hosts/fstab block and retains the old volatile layout.
startup_blockers.required_change: In managed mode preserve Ubuntu /etc, /etc/fstab, machine-id, apt/keyring configs, passwd/group/shadow, ld.so paths/cache and /var/lib/{dpkg,apt}. Create only explicitly owned ASUS runtime files under /run/asus or vendor directories; maintain /var/run -> /run and sticky /tmp. Give ASUS generated hosts/DNS/account changes explicit owners and merge/replace only the owned records, rather than importing /rom/etc wholesale.
startup_blockers.qualification: mkdir calls alone do not delete existing package state. The destructive writes and legacy volatile layout assumptions are the blockers; their exact active board paths still require tests.

startup_blockers.evidence: Early rc mounts API filesystems and init_main mounts /data then loads bcm_knvram before sysinit; later it prepares JFFS and certificates.
startup_blockers.required_change: systemd/initramfs own API and durable root/data mounts. Enter and authenticate manager mode before early mount/module actions. Preserve board-specific NVRAM, JFFS, certificate and hardware ordering behind explicit ready dependencies; do not remount a filesystem over active /run sockets or /var databases. The reused mount helper is only partial protection and does not catch shell mount commands or file writes.

startup_blockers.evidence: Stock shutdown broadcasts TERM/KILL and directly reboots; reboothalt_main signals PID1 and forks a delayed SysRq reset fallback.
startup_blockers.required_change: Ubuntu-only reboot/halt requests go to authenticated broker/systemd; rc waits for ordered stop, drains ASUS hardware, and exits. Eliminate global kill(-1), raw reboot and delayed SysRq reset from this managed build. Original standalone ASUS firmware remains a separate build, never a fallback selected by missing marker. Order ASUS drain before durable data unmount; no unbounded crash reinitialization.

startup_blockers.evidence: Current ARMEL libshared exports all seven notify_rc API names. BE98 preserves libshared notification/NVRAM behavior and only retargets its synchronous kill(1,SIGUSR1) edge while inside those APIs.
startup_blockers.required_change: Build the correct ARMEL shim and use explicit linking or selected ASUS process launchers. Native broker has its own arm64 dependency; do not pass a native arm64 preload to an ARMEL child. Missing shim or broker fails closed in managed mode. No global LD_PRELOAD, /etc/ld.so.preload, getpid override or blanket kill rewrite is allowed. The Ubuntu-specific client and shim now also fail closed when the management marker is absent; no production-only legacy fallback remains.
startup_blockers.tested_now: Native ARM64 mock call shape only; not actual BE19000AI libshared/NVRAM queue behavior or concurrency.

startup_blockers.evidence: ai_reboot explicitly toggles AISOM reboot GPIO; ai_upgrade/requests transfer control data; start_ai_service starts response checking and the AI tftpd endpoint (169.254.0.1, /ai). Stopping the AI service stops those BCM daemons, not the AI board OS.
startup_blockers.required_change: Preserve /ai firmware/docker_images/ctrl_msg/log ownership, AI IPC/keys/control and the internal endpoint. Port AI manager predicates. Keep AI reboot/upgrade as separate explicit actions; do not invoke them during Wi-Fi/web/ordinary port service restarts. Do not translate the BCM broker power operation into a combined BCM+AI reset.

Preserve Ubuntu /bin/sh (dash) and use a vendor-private BusyBox ash with explicit shebang/callsite for unconverted ASUS scripts. Audit command/app option behavior as well as syntax. system()/popen() strings still select libc /bin/sh and ignore SHELL; rebuild relevant rc call sites to explicit private-shell argv or verified POSIX strings. Do not solve this by replacing global /bin/sh, PATH, or global libc/preload interposition.
startup_blockers.prepared_elsewhere: The closure agent prepared two scoped ai_upgrade == to = patches, for pinned source and distinct extracted rootfs helper. This is not a complete shell migration.

must_not: receive raw ASUS SIGUSR1 as notification
have its /run or durable /var replaced by sysinit
reset all interfaces for unrelated web/service changes
rewrite Ubuntu conffiles or package database

owns: exactly one daemon instance and its child cgroup
must_not: order After=asus-rc when synchronously started before rc READY

owns: its own OS, containers and reboot lifecycle
must_not: be rebooted as a generic side effect of BCM Wi-Fi/web/port restart

be98_reuse_and_corrections.reuse: Explicit manager identity, root peer authentication, direct-child handshake, fixed protocol, restricted signals, subreaper and ordered drain. Source/recipe reused, no stale binary copied.
be98_reuse_and_corrections.not_drop_in: Its volatile /tmp/etc assumptions and hardcoded BE98 trial guard do not implement Ubuntu persistent layout or BE19000AI board guard.

be98_reuse_and_corrections.reuse: One daemon owner, fixed argv records with no shell evaluation, supervisor follows owned children, service split leaves hardware policy in rc.
be98_reuse_and_corrections.not_drop_in: The 23-unit split is a later stage; closed hostapd objects, board conditionals and AI service ownership differ. The checkpoint explicitly requires later dashboard/AiMesh fixes.

be98_reuse_and_corrections.required_regression: netdev_calc used a null strchr result for wlN names and an invalid snprintf bound; port robust interface parsing while preserving fortify. A startup migration must not restore the pre-fix crash.

Preserve fixed-width legacy shared-memory protocol time fields while application time64 remains enabled; measure BE19000AI cfg/networkmap producer layout rather than copying BE98 struct sizes. Keep bounded MAC formatters, valid empty JSON behavior and processed localization tags.

be98_reuse_and_corrections.open_reference_issue: acsd2 had one initial automatic restart and the precise cause was not proven. Slow daemonization/handoff timing must be measured again, not presented as already solved for this board.

changes_from_reference: Private compile-time path overrides for isolated fixtures
Reject unused nonzero request fields and duplicate READY
Remove BE98-specific ARMEL trial guard injection and clear broker process-local LD_PRELOAD before child exec
Ubuntu-only client unconditionally rejects missing marker with ENOTCONN and has no direct kill(1)/reboot fallback in any build.
Manager entry rejects PID1 and missing marker; manager identity/readiness/shutdown/mount and broker requests fail closed when the marker disappears.
Notify APIs reject a missing marker before original API invocation; the scoped kill(1,SIGUSR1) edge always goes through marker-checked broker exchange, including marker-loss races.
rc-only linker wrappers always broker PID1 requests and reject kill(-1), independently of marker; ordinary other-PID signals retain passthrough.
Offline broker builds additionally remove real power execution; normal client/manager/shim/wrapper logic is tested separately without LEON_RC_OFFLINE_TEST using inert physical-call counters.
new_foundation.deployment_limit: Built with host GCC16.1.0; these artifacts are NOT the accepted Ubuntu GCC16.2/glibc2.44 deployment binaries. Rebuild from these sources in that accepted environment; also build ARMEL and optional ARMHF shims with matched runtime closure. No unit or preload configuration was installed.

validation.identity: Actual root and uid65534 peers inside a private user namespace; disposable socket permissions relaxed only to prove SO_PEERCRED rejection.
validation.power_scope: Private text receipt only. No systemctl power command or real reboot syscall executed. All delivered signals target owned fixtures or the caller itself.
not_acceptance: systemd PID1 unit ordering with this broker

checks: seven notify APIs rejected before original invocation
rc-only PID1 and broadcast wrappers rejected
zero physical-call counters for prohibited actions
ordinary other-PID passthrough reaches only inert counter
normal broker refuses entry without marker
running broker and mock manager reject marker loss without power request

minimum_next_source_work: Capture exact BE19000AI rc compile configuration, include files, selected prebuilt objects and linker inputs at the pinned source revision. rc Makefile chooses model/SDK-specific prebuilt hostapd/WPS objects and has a separate ai_service.o path; do not link old BE98 object files.

Wire the role/client/manager helpers into current rc before any early /data/NVRAM effects, replace active manager checks (including ai_service.c), and audit retained object kill/reboot references under narrow linker wrappers.

Implement a managed sysinit ownership branch for persistent Ubuntu filesystems/accounts/DNS, with regression sentinels proving /etc/fstab, machine-id, apt config and /var/lib/dpkg survive start/stop/restart.

Port managed shutdown gate and eliminate global signal/direct SysRq/reboot paths only for managed mode; retain standalone ASUS behavior only in its separate original build, never as a missing-marker fallback.

Provide scoped per-ABI notification shim linkage/launchers and private ASUS shell call paths, then rebuild with accepted candidate toolchain and all required ARMEL libraries. No full rc compile/link was attempted by this foundation task.
Reuse later web/AiMesh fixes against actual AI producer contracts; retain time64 default with explicit legacy protocol fields.

Only after offline actual-binary/QEMU acceptance, introduce disabled package-owned units and prove one daemon owner, then perform the root task hardware acceptance gate before any flash. Packaging stock files alone is not startup acceptance.

resolved_review_findings.description: Original BE98-derived production branch selected raw kill(1)/reboot when management marker was missing, while only offline macro blocked it. Related manager, notify and rc-only wrapper paths also retained legacy behavior.
resolved_review_findings.resolution: Removed legacy fallback unconditionally in the Ubuntu-specific copied foundation and added normal-logic plus running-marker-loss regression tests. Actual board rc remains unmodified and unaccepted.
